review.method: acceptance suite run locally with the retail capability; this harness derives every field from the recorded log, production discovery of $CS_GAME_DIR, the production baseline report over that installation, the production ROF mount of GOSDATA/ASSETS/crimson.rof and the production F38-B host-call scanner over the three chapter-construction members, rustc and Cargo.lock; validated with tools/validate_evidence.py --require-pass. The consumer trace is cs_content::catalog::baseline::retail_baseline + baseline_report_json, the same functions `cs-inspect catalog --cs-path` writes. The measurement verifies three members of GOSDATA/ASSETS/crimson.rof byte-for-byte: ASSETS/SCRIPTS/CAMPAIGNINTRO.SCRIPT (a callback site stating native id 2151 and the "chap" conv$(FC) ".mpg" construction), ASSETS/SCRIPTS/CTL.SCRIPT (movie CL, the "assets\\graphics\\mpg\\" BL resolution, loop CL, getstatus(CL)) and ASSETS/SCRIPTS/PASSENGERCABIN.SCRIPT (the same 2151 site, the FC != 0 gate and script_run "campaignintro.script"); the hashed chapter-members.json artifact records each member's decoded sha256, site spans and fragment offsets. A file whose name spells the construction's product shape (chap + digits + .mpg) and that no record of either naming source reaches is counted under chapter_name_unbound in addition to unnamed_video_file, and every unverifiable member under chapter_source_unreadable with the member named in the diagnostic. No row is minted for chap1 through chap5: the construction states no name until FC is bound, and FC's domain is the return of a native callback that no installation byte states. LIMITATION: Which values FC takes — and so which chapter number each chap<N>.mpg file belongs to — is the return domain of native callback 2151, engine state no installation byte states: the scripts show the FC != 0 gate and the "chap" conv$(FC) ".mpg" construction, the ZBD tree shows chapter directories C1 through C5, and the decrypted engine's string table spells chap1.mpg through chap6.mpg adjacent, but none of those bind a value to a file. Affected content: chap1.mpg through chap5.mpg, counted under chapter_name_unbound. Resolving evidence: an original-run capture of the callback's domain, which agents cannot produce (human/original-run only).
